title: Garlic Butter Pasta
description: A quick, comforting weeknight pasta made by melting garlic and butter into olive oil, then tossing it with spaghetti, starchy pasta water, and parmesan for a glossy, clinging sauce.

ingredients.sourceText: put a big pot of water on to boil, salt it generously
take about, let's say two hundred grams of spaghetti, we'll cook that later
add a good glug of olive oil, just eyeball it
take four cloves of garlic, minced, and let that go in the oil until it's fragrant
now add two tablespoons of butter — actually you know what, make it three, I like it really buttery
oh also grab some red pepper flakes if you have them, totally optional but I love the heat
make sure you save a cup of that starchy pasta water before you drain it
now stir in the parmesan, get it nice and glossy
season with salt and black pepper to taste
finish with a handful of chopped parsley

steps.text: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil.
Once boiling, add the spaghetti and cook according to package directions, about 9 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a good glug of olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and cook in the oil until fragrant, about a minute.
Add the butter and let it melt into the oil and garlic, swirling the pan so it doesn't burn.
Stir in red pepper flakes, if using.
Before draining, reserve a cup of the starchy pasta water. Drain the spaghetti when it's about a minute from done.
Add the drained spaghetti straight into the garlic butter pan along with a splash of the reserved pasta water, and toss to combine.
Stir in the parmesan until the sauce looks glossy, adding another splash of pasta water if it looks dry.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste, and finish with chopped parsley.
Remove the pan from the heat and let it sit for about 30 seconds before plating so the sauce firms up and clings better.
Plate the pasta, topping with extra parmesan and cracked pepper.

tips.text: The starch in the reserved pasta water is what makes the sauce cling to the noodles instead of pooling at the bottom.
If the garlic starts browning too fast, pull the pan off the heat for a second to keep it from burning.

warnings.message: Parmesan has no specified amount; source only says 'stir in the parmesan'.
Olive oil amount is imprecise ('a good glug of olive oil, just eyeball it').
Parsley amount is imprecise ('a handful of chopped parsley').
Salt quantity for the pot is imprecise ('salt it generously').
Red pepper flakes have no specified amount, even though they're listed as an ingredient.
